items.title: Find the main idea
items.text:
A. The club meets every Wednesday to repair broken household objects. Last month, students fixed lamps and chairs that would otherwise have been thrown away. Visitors bring an item and learn to repair it with help from volunteers.
B. You do not need to buy expensive equipment to enjoy our group. Members exchange books and discuss one chapter each week. Anyone can suggest the next title, and new readers are welcome even if they have not finished the book.
C. Our volunteers visit a local animal shelter on Saturdays. They prepare food, clean the cages and play with the dogs. Before starting, everyone attends a short safety session led by the shelter staff.
D. Members spend an hour outdoors before school, observing local birds. They keep a shared record of what they see, including the place and the weather. The records help scientists understand how the area changes through the seasons.
E. The group turns unused land into a vegetable garden. Members learn when to plant seeds and how to save water. Part of the harvest goes to the school kitchen, while the rest is donated to neighbours.
F. Our members produce a monthly programme for the school radio. They choose topics, interview guests and edit recordings. The most important rule is to check every fact before a story is broadcast.
G. This club helps pupils practise conversations in other languages. Instead of following a textbook, students play short scenes such as asking for directions. Mistakes are discussed after the conversation, so speakers are not interrupted.
items.why: Смысловые опоры: A repair → 3; B books → 6; C shelter → 4; D records/birds → 7; E vegetable garden → 1; F radio/fact checking → 5; G conversations → 2.

items.title: The book exchange
items.text:
In September, twelve pupils at Westbrook School decided to organise a book exchange. The school library already had enough textbooks, but students wanted to share books they had chosen themselves. They first suggested holding the event in the playground. However, the head teacher pointed out that rain could damage the books, so the group chose the assembly hall instead.
At first, the pupils planned to exchange one book for another. They soon realised that this would exclude students who had no suitable books to bring. To solve the problem, the organisers gave everyone a free ticket for their first book. Extra tickets could be earned by helping to arrange the room. No money was collected.
The event opened at half past ten on a Saturday. Although only twenty visitors were expected, more than fifty arrived before lunchtime. Several parents offered to donate books, but the organisers asked them to wait until the next event because the tables were already full. The most popular books were adventure stories; poetry attracted a smaller but enthusiastic group of readers.
Afterwards, the students collected anonymous comments. Most visitors wanted another exchange, although some suggested a quieter corner for discussing books. The organisers decided to include one next time. They also planned a shelf for books in different languages. They did not agree on a date for the next exchange, as the school calendar had not yet been published.

speaking.title: Чтение вслух · демоверсия
speaking.text: Bicycles or bikes are an important means of transportation in many parts of the world. The first bicycles turned up in Europe in the first half of the 19th century but the word “bicycle” only appeared later, in 1868. There are more bicycles in the world than cars. A lot of people have realized that cycling is an easy way to get around and a great way to cut down on pollution. More and more cities have special places where people can borrow a bike and ride around the city. Over the past few years, a bicycle infrastructure has been created in Moscow. Cycling in the centre of Moscow in summer is one of the most pleasant and quickest ways of seeing the city.

speaking.title: Чтение вслух · демоверсия
speaking.text: Land pollution has its effect on people, animals and plants. That is why it is very important to stop land pollution as quickly as possible. Fortunately, there are several possible solutions to the land pollution problem, including conservation. For instance, we can leave old trees in a forest to naturally die instead of cutting them down. We must also process waste and dispose of it in the safest manner possible not to create huge landfills with tons of plastic. We should stop using so much plastic. Even if you stop buying plastic shopping bags each time you go shopping for food, and get a cloth bag instead, this simple step will make a difference. Instead of throwing something away, think about a way to reuse or recycle it. You can turn to organic gardening practices as well and stop using dangerous chemicals in your garden. Fighting land pollution needs everyone’s effort.

speaking.title: Urban gardens
speaking.text: Urban gardens are becoming common in many cities. People grow vegetables on roofs, balconies and small pieces of unused land. These gardens can provide fresh food, but their value is not limited to the harvest. Neighbours who rarely spoke before begin to work together. Children discover how plants develop and why water matters. Some gardens also collect rainwater and create safe places for insects. Starting a garden requires careful planning. People need to check the quality of the soil, find suitable plants and agree on a watering schedule. Not every attempt succeeds immediately, especially when the weather is unusual. However, sharing the work helps the group solve problems. Even a small garden can change the way people feel about the place where they live.

writing.title: Choosing books
writing.text:
Imagine that you are doing a project on what helps teenagers in Zetland choose a book. You have found a survey (see table). Comment on the data and give your opinion. Write 200–250 words.

Make an opening statement on the subject. Select and report 2–3 facts. Make 1–2 comparisons and give your comments. Outline a problem that can arise when choosing a book and suggest a solution. Conclude by giving and explaining your opinion on the importance of reading for teenagers.
